target_constraint: Must prevent biofilm formation on implant surfaces
observed_phenomenon: Surgical site infection following spinal fusion
mechanism: Bioactive mesoporous silica nanoparticles loaded with plant extracts exhibit antibiofilm activity against biofilm-forming Staphylococcus aureus, a common pathogen in surgical site infections.
intervention: Coat the spinal fusion device (e.g., 3D-printed porous titanium cage) with a surface layer of mesoporous silica nanoparticles loaded with Onosma armenum extract, applied via dip-coating or spray deposition, to release antibiofilm phytochemicals locally at the implant–tissue interface.
expected_effect: Prevention of Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation on the implant surface, reducing the incidence of surgical site infection following spinal fusion without relying solely on systemic antibiotic prophylaxis.
falsification_test: In an in vitro biofilm assay, incubate coated and uncoated spinal fusion implant coupons with Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923 for 48 hours, then quantify viable biofilm biomass via crystal violet staining or colony-forming unit counts; the candidate is falsified if coated coupons show no significant reduction in biofilm formation compared to uncoated controls.
source_spans: "bioactive mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNPs) loaded with Onosma armenum extract were developed to evaluate their antibiofilm activity against biofilm-forming Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923"
